BEFORE #3510's fix, an xmlport living in a precompiled dependency raised NavMetadataNotFoundException from inside its own constructor (NavXmlPort.BeginInitialization -> NCLMetadata.GetMetaXmlPortById -> RecordPatches.NCLMetadata_GetMetaApplicationObjectByType), because BuildNCLMetaXmlPort's existence check read _parsedXmlPorts -- the AL-SOURCE parser's dictionary -- and so returned null for every xmlport the runner did not itself compile. That is a .NET exception BC does not model as an AL error: it is not catchable with asserterror and aborts the whole test. Measured on BC 28.1.49838.53910 against a real Microsoft Base Application, it hit 44 of 44 precompiled xmlports -- the entire population AL can see, not the six ids #3510 happened to observe through Microsoft's test buckets. AFTER the fix the metadata object builds and BeginInitialization proceeds one layer deeper, to ask for the xmlport's node schema, which the runner genuinely does not have: a shipped .app carries src/ and SymbolReference.json and no compiled metadata document, and the symbol file states an xmlport's Properties and Variables but no node tree at all (measured: BC 28.1's Base Application SymbolReference.json has a top-level "XmlPorts": [] with all 40 of its xmlports nested under "Namespaces", each carrying only Id, Name, Properties, Variables, Methods and ReferenceSourceFileName, while BC's own emitted documents for four such xmlports carry 91 <Node> elements between them). RunnerXmlMetadataLoader therefore refuses by name -- RunnerOutOfScopeException on INCLObjectXmlMetadataLoader.GetMetaObjectXmlMetadata(XmlPort 61602), reason not-yet-implemented -- rather than handing back an empty document that would let the port silently export nothing. WHY expect-oos AND NOT expect-fail-known-gap: the result IS a typed out-of-scope signal with a reason anchor, which is what expect-oos means; expect-fail-known-gap accepts any non-pass result and would therefore also accept the pre-fix NavMetadataNotFoundException, making the entry unable to tell the two boundaries apart -- which is the one thing it exists to do. Deriving the node schema for a precompiled xmlport is tracked by #3797 (the runner derives no xmlport metadata beyond (id, name)); the shape it would follow is DependencyReportMetadata.cs, which already reconstructs a precompiled dependency REPORT's document from the .app. That issue stays OPEN after #3510 merges.
